images.caption:
Lions resting in the Virunga National Park, near the Rwindi Station.
The Virunga National Park (formerly Albert National Park) lies from the Virunga Mountains, to the Rwenzori Mountains, in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, bordering Volcanoes National Park in Rwanda and Rwenzori Mountains National Park in Uganda. 
The lion (Panthera leo) is one of four big cats in the genus Panthera, and a member of the family Felidae. They typically inhabit savanna and grassland, although they may take to bush and forest. Lions are unusually social compared to other cats.  The lion is an apex and keystone predator, although they will scavenge if the opportunity arises. 

Digitized slide.

images.filename: Lava flowing from the Murara volcano.jpg
images.caption:
Murara was a small, short-lived, cinder cone on the flank of Mount Nyamuragira, that began erupting on December 23, 1976. Eruptions from Murara reduced considerably after the eruption of Mount Nyiragongo on January 10, 1977 and ended completely in April 1977.
Photo taken at time of maximum activity, two days before the Nyiragongo eruption.

images.caption:

Photo taken at time of maximum activity, two days before the Nyiragongo eruption and just before nightfall.

Temporary camp in foreground was organised for visitors by the Virunga National Park authority.
